correctness.rationale: Real Fourier cosine/sine normalization yields a 4×3 analysis matrix whose normalized Gram blocks as scalar η and a 2×2 positive matrix with trace T=4+2(1+q²)(1+c), determinant 4(1−q)²(1+c). Thus positive eigenvalues iff −1<c<1. η decreases strictly, μ− increases strictly on [−1,1], giving a single crossing; the crossing quadratic has exactly one positive root cstar∈(1/2,1). Its Taylor expansion gives 1−cstar∼(1−q)²/6; unimodality gives exact two-neighbor finite-grid search. Independent construction of 105 different 4×3 matrices reproduced all three Gram eigenvalues. Finite tests not mistaken for proof across N,t.
residual_risks: Optimizes lowest frame eigenvalue in raw unweighted sample norm, not mean-square error, noisy inverse or finite-time sampling design beyond two levels.

final_claim: For N>=5, first 3 Fourier modes on cycle and four raw unweighted samples from 2 distinct vertices at times 0,t>0, exact Gram spectrum has η=2(1+q²)(1-c), μ±=(T±sqrt(T²−16(1−q)²(1+c)))/2; the sharp continuous-angle lower-frame optimum is at unique cstar(q)∈(1/2,1), q=e^(-tλ1), and every discrete optimal offset brackets cstar on the cycle cosine grid.
limitations: No claim of optimal noise variance, arbitrary weights or higher-bandwidth design
